sections.title: Announcement returns
sections.question: How does the stock react when the board fires the CEO, and does it matter who and why?
sections.interpretation: Over trading days -1 to +1, forced exits earn -2.3% (t = -5.18, N = 528) and retirements -0.3%. Fired founders earn -3.2% against -2.2% (gap p 0.627). Firings over a personal scandal earn -1.5%, other firings -2.3% (gap p 0.317). Prices fall -5.4% over days -30 to -2 and are flat over days +2 to +60 (-1.0%).

methodology.test: Cross-sectional t, Boehmer-Musumeci-Poulsen standardized t, Wilcoxon signed-rank; Welch t and Mann-Whitney U for differences
methodology.data: Daily total returns; market model estimated over trading days -250 to -30 for days -1 to +1; market-adjusted returns for longer windows
methodology.caveat: Day 0 is the first trading day on or after the announcement that the CEO is leaving. Firings for fraud or crime are not in the sample. Reasons other than the hand-checked conduct labels are model codes.

sections.title: Long-run returns
sections.question: Does the firm do better or worse in the 12, 36 and 60 months after the firing?
sections.interpretation: Against the market, the median forced-exit firm returns -6.3% over 12 months, -15.3% over 36 and -32.1% over 60. Against a matched firm the medians are -4.6%, 0.0% and -4.7%.

rows: Panel A. Median return minus the market
Panel B. Median return minus a matched firm
tables.notes: Medians of buy-and-hold returns from day +2 over 12, 36 and 60 months, all firings, with the Wilcoxon p. Panel A subtracts the market's buy-and-hold return; Panel B subtracts a matched firm in the same industry, with market value within 30 percent and the nearest return on assets. N, 36m counts events at 36 months.

tables.title: Table IA.10. Calendar-time alpha after the announcement
rows: Fired over a personal scandal, 36 months
tables.notes: Each calendar month the portfolio holds every firm whose announcement fell 1 to H months before. Its return minus the risk-free rate is regressed on the Fama-French five factors and momentum; alpha is the intercept, with Newey-West t (6 lags). Value weights are market values at the fiscal year-end before the event. Months with fewer than 10 firms are dropped. The difference rows regress the firing portfolio's return minus the retirement portfolio's. Delisted firms take their delisting return in their last month.
